identity.name: Tabal
native_names: Bit-Burutas (Assyrian name after the c. 718 reorganisation)

land.text: the Tabalian region, which the Neo-Hittite states page lists in the northern group: Kammanu (with Melid), Hilakku, Hiyawa, Gurgum, Kummuh and Carchemish

predecessors.note: The Neo-Hittite states page gives no date or history for Tabal; Cliopatria's Neo-Hittite row (-1150..-801) borders Tabal in -900..-801.

land.text: Tabal's land, an Assyrian province (Bit-Burutas) from 713

successors.note: Infobox 'Annexation by the Neo-Assyrian Empire: 713 BC'. After Sargon II's death in 705 the region 'becoming independent again' and reappears as a single kingdom under Esarhaddon (Tabal page); no dossier covers that revival.

capitals.name: Artulu (site not fixed; Kayseri region)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Artulu'. The page gives the name only; the coordinates are the gazetteer's Kayseri, the centre of the land the page names. Artulu is not in the gazetteer (listed for it).

keyframe_review.note: Reviewer fix, shape re-checked on the gazetteer: Cliopatria's 38,587 km2 shape (34.5-38.1 E, 36.6-38.8 N), -900..-751, lies in Cilicia and the Anti-Taurus, not on the page's land: of its 137 cells 52 are in Adana, 51 in Kahramanmaras, 11 in Osmaniye, 7 in Mersin, 5 in Malatya, 4 in Sivas and only 3 in Kayseri, none in Nevsehir or Nigde. The Tabal page (re-read 2026-10-19) puts the kingdom 'in the modern Turkish provinces of Kayseri, Nevşehir, and Niğde', 'consolidating its power in northwestern Cappadocia', and does not mention Cilicia; it calls Tabal 'one of the several states located in the larger region of Tabal' and says the Assyrians used the name 'in a narrow sense to refer to the kingdom of Tabal'. So the verdict is wrong (not the reviewer's adjust: 3 of 137 cells overlap the page's land) and the correction is the three provinces (about 27,000 km2 on the gazetteer's cells, against Cliopatria's 34,647 on the same cells: ratio 0.8, within a factor of two, but in another place). The page gives no infobox area. The first dated fact on the page is 837 (Shalmaneser III), so -900..-838 is unverified.

correction.text: Tabal proper, 'in the modern Turkish provinces of Kayseri, Nevşehir, and Niğde', 'consolidating its power in northwestern Cappadocia'

Tabal proper in the three provinces of Kayseri, Nevşehir and Niğde, held to 713 instead of 701; 'deported Ambaris, his family and his chief courtiers to Assyria in 713 BCE', after which Bit-Burutas became an Assyrian province.

keyframe_review.note: -750..-701, the same Cliopatria shape as -900 (38,587 km2) and wrong for the same reason (Cilicia and Kahramanmaras, 3 of 137 cells in Kayseri), so the correction is the three provinces as for -900. The Tabal page has Sargon II annex the kingdom (Bit-Burutas) in 713 (infobox 'Annexation by the Neo-Assyrian Empire: 713 BC'), so the Tabal shape ends in 713; after Sargon's death in 705 the region is 'independent again' but the page names no kingdom until Esarhaddon (681-669). Years: -750..-713.

region.text: the land around Kayseri, in the modern provinces of Kayseri, Nevsehir and Nigde

ledger.note: 900 (page silent): Tabal in Cappadocia. The Tabal page gives no founding year; its first dated fact is Tuwattis I's surrender to Shalmaneser III in 837. The year is Cliopatria's; the Neo-Hittite states page says only that such states 'arose following the collapse of the Hittite New Kingdom in the 12th century BCE'.

region.text: Tabal proper, tributary to the Neo-Assyrian king

ledger.note: c. 738: Tabal becomes a tributary of Assyria. 'By c. 738 BC, the Tabalian region, including Tabal proper, had become a tributary of the Neo-Assyrian king' (infobox 'Submission to the Neo-Assyrian Empire: c. 740 BC'; 'Vassal of the Neo-Assyrian Empire (c. 740s - 713 BC)'). Tabal is the vassal and neo-assyrian-empire the suzerain; the wider Tabalian region (the page: Tabal was 'one of the several states located in the larger region of Tabal') was tributary too but has no dossier; mirrors a vassal_start that neo-assyrian-empire (me-02) should add with counterpart tabal-kingdom (reviewer fix). The earlier tribute of 837-836 is in /wars/0 only.

c. 718: Tabal is reorganised into Bit-Burutas. Infobox 'Reorganisation into Bīt-Burutaš: c. 718 BC'; Sargon II restored Ḫullî in 721 and 'soon appointed Ḫullî's son Ambaris as his successor to the kingship of Tabal'. Same state, same colour.

region.text: Tabal proper, tributary to the Neo-Assyrian king

ledger.note: 713: the tribute ends in annexation. After the deportation of Ambaris, 'Bīt-Burutaš was annexed into the Neo-Assyrian Empire and made into a province' (infobox 'Annexation by the Neo-Assyrian Empire: 713 BC'; vassal 'c. 740s - 713 BC'); the land itself passes in the loss below. Mirrors the vassal_end that neo-assyrian-empire (me-02) should add with counterpart tabal-kingdom (reviewer fix).

713: Sargon II annexes Tabal. 'likely beginning in 714 BC, Ambaris came under pressure from Midas' of Phrygia; Sargon 'consequently deported Ambaris, his family and his chief courtiers to Assyria in 713 BCE', after which Bit-Burutas became an Assyrian province (infobox 'Annexation by the Neo-Assyrian Empire: 713 BC'). Region corrected to the three provinces (see /keyframe_review/0); neo-assyrian-empire /ledger/24 draws the same gain on Cliopatria's Tabal shape, which lies mostly in Adana and Kahramanmaras.

713: the Tabal kingdom ends. 'In 705 BCE, Sargon II campaigned against the Cimmerians in Tabal but he died in battle against one Gurdî of Kulummu', which ended Assyrian direct rule and made the region independent again; Cliopatria's row runs to -701 but no page names a kingdom between 705 and Esarhaddon's reign (the revival is not in this dossier).

wars.name: Shalmaneser III's Tabalian campaign
wars.outcome: Tuwattis I surrendered when the Assyrian army surrounded his city; the kings of Tabal offered tribute again in 836.
wars.note: Tabal as a tributary c. 738-713 is the vassal_start/vassal_end pair in /ledger; the tribute of 837-836 ('the kings of Tabal offered tribute again in 836') is recorded here only. The Shalmaneser III page (opened 2026-10-19 for the reviewer's thin note) dates 'In 836 BC ... an expedition against the Tibareni (Tabal)' and nothing earlier.

wars.name: Tiglath-pileser III's subjugation of Tabal
wars.outcome: By c. 738 the Tabalian region was a tributary of the Neo-Assyrian king; c. 732-730 Tiglath-pileser deposed Wasusarmas and installed Hulli.
wars.note: This is the standing tributary relation recorded as vassal_start -738 and vassal_end -713 in /ledger.

wars.name: Sargon II's annexation of Bit-Burutas

zones.text: the land around Kayseri, in the modern provinces of Kayseri, Nevsehir and Nigde

wars.outcome: Ambaris, pressed by Midas of Phrygia from c. 714, was deported in 713 and Bit-Burutas annexed as an Assyrian province.
wars.note: Shalmaneser V deported Hulli in 726; Sargon II restored him in 721 and appointed his son Ambaris.

certainty.note: No page gives a Tabalian border. The extent is Tabal proper in the provinces of Kayseri, Nevşehir and Niğde (the Tabal page); Cliopatria's shape is not used (see /keyframe_review/0).

notes:
Page budget 1-2 pages: the Tabal (state) and Neo-Hittite states pages were opened; the second added no dates. After the review the Tabal page was re-read and the Shalmaneser III page opened (outside the budget, for the thin note: it gives 836 only). No area on any page.

Review repair (2026-10-19): (1) Added vassal_start -738 and vassal_end -713 (counterpart neo-assyrian-empire); me-02 should add the mirror with counterpart tabal-kingdom. (2) The Cliopatria shape was found not to be an over-wide Tabal but a shape in the wrong place (3 of 137 cells in Kayseri; the rest in Adana, Kahramanmaras, Osmaniye, Mersin, Malatya, Sivas), so both keyframes are 'wrong' with the three-province correction, and the loss, dissolve and successor regions use the same three provinces; neo-assyrian-empire /ledger/24 still draws its 713 gain on Cliopatria's shape and should use the three provinces. The reviewer asked for 'adjust'; 'wrong' is the schema's word for a shape that should not be used.

Open points: (1) Nothing is dated before 836-837 (Tabal page and Shalmaneser III page); the founding year -900 stays Cliopatria's, confidence 1; a gap-filler should read the Seshat page (tr_tabal_k). (2) Cliopatria's Tabal row runs to -701 and the page's annexation is 713; the kingdom ends here in 713. The region was independent again after 705 and reappears 'as a single kingdom under Esarhaddon' with rulers Iskallu and Mugallu; a dossier for post-705 Tabal may be needed, no page opened dates its end. (3) The capital Artulu is not in the gazetteer; the capital dot uses Kayseri. Names for the gazetteer: Artulu (Tabal capital, near Kayseri), Kammanu, Hilakku (Cilicia), Hiyawa.
